A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HELVIPAD dataset and 360-IGEV-Stereo work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original stereo benchmarks, depth-completion evaluations, ablations and cross-dataset fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds boundary-consistency measurements, Stereo-SF3D transfer results and an external qualitative example.

M1.justification: The mapping and depth-completion algorithms, polar-map encoder, vertical cost-volume construction and circular-padding procedure remain unchanged. Revised disparity bounds and search limits are experimental parameter changes rather than new algorithmic components.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds Stereo-SF3D evaluation and zero-shot inference on one unlabeled external real-world image. HELVIPAD and Stereo-MP3D remain. A.1 changes the sequence count from 29 to 26, but the unchanged sequence listing in Table 4 does not establish removed coverage.

E2.justification: The expanded transfer study adds a Stereo-MP3D-pretrained 360SD-Net comparator for Stereo-SF3D alongside random and HELVIPAD initialization (v2 Table 14). The main stereo baselines and the temporal-aggregation comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 changes 360-IGEV-Stereo's reported disparity clamp from 0.062–14.75 degrees to 0.048–23 degrees and its cost-volume maximum disparity from 96 to 128 pixels. v2 also introduces LRCE evaluation using depth-completed test labels and supplements the selected-point calibration assessment with 200 randomly selected points. These disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative boundary-consistency analysis across models, ablation variants and scene types, plus a random-point calibration check and an external zero-shot case study. Existing depth-completion sensitivity analyses, temporal-aggregation comparisons and cross-scene studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance. The uncertainty-based depth-completion filtering and point-estimate reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Central benchmark, ablation, pretraining and plotted scene results change beyond rounding. For example, 360-IGEV-Stereo's Table 2 depth MAE changes from 1.77 to 1.720 m alongside revised settings, so this is not a controlled performance gain. New results include LRCE, the 1.7-pixel random-point calibration error, Stereo-SF3D transfer and external-image predictions. Retained Stereo-MP3D rows mainly gain numerical precision.

T1.justification: The geometric equations, interpolation and filtering derivations, and padding definition retain their mathematical substance. The projection formula moves into Algorithm 1. Appendix D.1 additionally explains the cited LRCE metric through its formula, without introducing a new theoretical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a real-world omnidirectional stereo dataset, depth-completed training labels, benchmarking and effective stereo-model adaptations. Wording changes and additional supporting evaluations do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits temporal aggregation for fast-moving objects such as cars and states that occlusions are not explicitly handled, arguing that the small baseline limits their impact. It also adds explanations linking boundary-consistency errors to lighting, texture and scene structure, and discusses transfer beyond campus environments.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 updates documented disparity hyperparameters, while Section 3.4 newly describes manual review for train/test scene overlap. Appendix D.1 explains the boundary-label availability motivating depth-completed ground truth for LRCE. Existing hardware, training-budget and code-access information is largely retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds substantive discussion and citations for Unsupervised OmniMVS, panoramic distortion handling and prior circular-padding approaches, including 360MonoDepth, Panoformer and Cylin-Painting. The paper's overall positioning remains a real-world dataset contribution with adaptations of existing stereo methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work paragraphs, qualitative discussion and conclusion receive localized rewriting and corrections. Appendix E gains a consistency subsection, and captions and references are edited. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain LRCE columns, a scene-wise consistency table is added, and the transfer table expands to two datasets. Figure 7 gains augmented disparity maps, Figure 19 adds an external example, and Figure 5 is redrawn. These are localized display changes within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: Additional boundary and transfer evaluations, calibration checking and explicit motion/occlusion limitations provide a limited overall benefit. Reporting inconsistencies constrain that benefit: Section 5.2 quotes a depth-MAE reduction from 1.81 to 1.77 m, whereas revised Table 2 gives 1.860 to 1.720 m; Appendix D.1 describes LRCE using disparity while tables report depth units. The added validation strengthens the paper modestly, but does not resolve its numerical documentation problems.
